clue.text: New women's group having split purpose? Not advisable

indicators.note: a word that has been split has had something pushed into its middle, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to put something to purpose is to use it
the WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women

explanation.surface: A newly formed women's society divided over its aims is told its plan is ill-judged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having split' tells you USE is opened up to take N and WI. The WI, Women's Institute, is a long-standing British network of local women's clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foolish or imprudent is the kind of course a sensible adviser would warn against.

clue.text: Distribution of beer to all that is easy to accept!

indicators.note: distributing things spreads them about, so the letters of these words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Handing out beer to everyone is a policy anyone could live with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distribution of' is the anagram signal over BEER TO ALL; 'that is' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bearable or passable is something one can put up with without complaint.

clue.text: Be naughty? Would I, likewise, be naughty ultimately?

parts.note: asking a question swaps the order of 'I would', so the contraction I'D is written the other way round
so means likewise, as in 'so do I'
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word naughty, its last letter

explanation.surface: A child, told to stop misbehaving, asks cheekily whether they would ever misbehave too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I would' shortens to I'D; the question form 'Would I' puts the two words the other way round, so the letters go in as DI. 'ultimately' takes Y, the last letter of 'naughty'.
explanation.definitionFit: To flout orders or rules is exactly how a mischievous child behaves badly.

clue.text: Bet securing high-class car would make you a happy character!

indicators.note: a bet securing something holds it fast inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to lay money is to bet it
RR is short for Rolls-Royce, the luxury car maker

explanation.surface: Winning a wager that lands you a luxury motor would leave anyone delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' puts RR, Rolls-Royce, inside LAY. 'Happy as Larry' is a British saying for someone completely contented.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom 'happy as Larry' makes this name the byword for a contented person.

clue.text: Bridge opponents left high-scoring card, causing tangle?

parts.note: at the bridge table East and North sit on opposing sides, so E and N face each other
an ace scores highest in most card games

explanation.surface: At the bridge table, one side plays a top card and the result is a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four seats are North, South, East and West, with North-South partnered against East-West, so E and N are opponents. 'causing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine or wrap threads around one another is to knot them together in a snarl.

clue.text: Company absorbed by one is in rising Mediterranean city

indicators.note: something absorbed by another is taken into its body, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down entry rising means the words are read from bottom to top, so they go backwards

parts.note: a means one, as in 'a pound'
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A business swallowed up by a single firm is located in a booming city by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns A IS IN round to NISIA, and 'absorbed by' then puts CO inside it after NI.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Cyprus lies on the island in the eastern part of that sea.

clue.text: A big star turning up for an Oscar?

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, so it reverses

parts.note: a draw is a big attraction, a star who pulls in crowds

explanation.surface: Will a famous actor appear to collect the Academy's statuette?
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses DRAW, a crowd-puller, to WARD after A. 'Turning up' at first looks like arriving at a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollywood's Academy statuette is the most famous prize in film.

clue.text: Energy yonder — one source of luminosity in the heavens

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
yonder means over there, in that place
a means one, as in 'a dozen'

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

explanation.surface: Energy far away, a single point of light glowing up in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' takes L, the first letter of 'luminosity'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airy and celestial, of the upper regions beyond the earth, belongs to the sky above.

clue.text: Ale — one carrying bone disease

indicators.note: a container carrying something holds it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
a rib is a bone of the chest
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Beer is blamed for a disease that attacks the skeleton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts RIB inside BEER to make BERIBER, then I is added. 'bone disease' looks like one phrase, but 'bone' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical illness caused by a lack of vitamin B1 is a deficiency ailment.

clue.text: Cartel wrath less activated by major economic collapse?

indicators.note: something activated is stirred into motion, so the letters of these words are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A business cartel, its fury spent, is jolted into action by a financial disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'activated' is the anagram signal over CARTEL WRATH LESS; 'by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1929 share-price crash on the New York stock market began the Great Depression.

clue.text: What could be tatty, namely, book bound in red?

parts.note: sc is short for scilicet, Latin for namely

indicators.note: a book bound in something is held within its covers, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ruby is a deep red colour

explanation.surface: Is a book bound in red leather the sort of thing that looks shabby?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound in' puts B inside RUBY, giving RUBBY after SC; 'What could be' only leads in to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby, stunted or scruffy things look worn and second-rate.

clue.text: Privileged member with batting team getting runs

parts.note: in cricket the team batting is said to be in
a side is a team
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A favoured club member scores runs while the batting side is in.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting team is 'in'; R stands for runs. 'with' and 'getting' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone within an organisation has access to information and favours outsiders lack.

clue.text: Leaders of Young Conservatives mobbing one in a gathering? It may lead to suspension

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one piece set in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for work or fun, as in a sewing bee

indicators.note: people mobbing someone crowd around them on every side, so the letters close round the next piece
the leaders of the words are their first letters

parts.note: an means one, as in 'an apple'

explanation.surface: Young Tory leaders surround someone at a party meeting, and a ban may follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders of' gives Y and C, 'mobbing' puts AN between them (YANC), and 'in' puts that inside A BEE. 'It may lead to' only points to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter held over is in a state of temporary disuse, put on hold for now.

clue.text: Another Phi? Means agonised discomfort, we hear

indicators.note: something agonised is twisted with pain, so the letters of the word are wrenched into a new order
says the word is judged by its sound when spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: an ache is a dull discomfort

explanation.surface: The setter wonders whether someone sharing his title means pain and distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agonised' rearranges MEANS to NAMES; 'we hear' turns ACHE into the same sound spelt AKE. Phi is the setter's own pseudonym, so another Phi is a person who shares that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bearing the same name as another person is that person's double in name only.

clue.text: Weapon to ensnare love-a scent

indicators.note: to ensnare something is to trap it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: arm means a weapon, as in firearm
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A weapon meant to trap a sweetheart turns out to be a fragrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ensnare' puts O, love as a tennis score, inside ARM; the A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant smell, such as that of coffee or baking, is a fragrance.

clue.text: Struggling to retain European position with regard to a certain line

definitions.text: position with regard to a certain line

indicators.note: struggling things writhe and twist, so these letters are wrestled into a new order

explanation.surface: Fighting to keep a European in place, someone lines things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggling' rearranges TO RETAIN into ORIENTAT, and E is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To align something by a compass bearing or reference line is to set its direction.

clue.text: Make version of sharper English?

indicators.note: making a new version of the letters means rewriting them in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone wants their English made crisper and asks for it to be rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make version of' rearranges SHARPER into REPHRAS before E, and the whole clue also describes the answer: rewording prose to make it crisper.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in different words is to produce a new wording of it.

clue.text: Editor, receiving pieces, has to edit

indicators.note: someone receiving something takes it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: chessmen are pieces, so men are pieces in board games

explanation.surface: An editor, handed some articles, has to revise them.
explanation.walkthrough: Pieces in chess and draughts are 'men'. 'receiving' puts MEN inside ED; 'has to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or revise a text is to improve it by careful changes.

clue.text: Forceful part of golf technique

definitions.meaning: forceful means vigorous and energetic, as with rain that lashes down
hitting long shots from the tee with a wooden club is one of a golfer's skills

explanation.definitionFit: The word means vigorous and powerful as an adjective, and as a noun the long hitting off the tee in golf.

clue.text: Keep principal one's invested in cash?

parts.note: main means principal or chief

indicators.note: something invested in another is placed inside it, as money is put into a fund

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money
a means one; here 'one's' is 'one is'

explanation.surface: The chief keeps his single holding in money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' puts A inside TIN, British slang for money, giving TAIN after MAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve or uphold something is to keep it going.

clue.text: Being cornered, runs, getting knocked about

indicators.note: something about another goes round it, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to tap is to knock lightly
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Caught in a corner, someone runs and gets roughed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TAPPED round R. 'knocked about' reads as one phrase for being beaten up, but 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stuck with no way out is caught, like an animal in a snare.

clue.text: Fires acceptable in revolutionary groups

indicators.note: one piece set in another is placed inside it
a revolution turns something right round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: sets are groups
OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: Fire-raising is tolerated among militant cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns SETS into STES, and 'in' puts OK inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tends a furnace feeds it fuel, keeping it burning.

clue.text: Electrical units-name used in SI here, possibly

indicators.note: a piece used in something is put inside it
possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A scientist checks whether a person's name appears among the standard units here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges SI HERE to HERIES, and 'used in' puts N inside it. SI is the International System of Units, where these units belong.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of inductance is named after the American physicist Joseph Henry.

clue.text: Fool about with saltpetre

parts.note: a nit is a fool, short for nitwit
re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: Someone foolish fiddles about with gunpowder ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate, used in gunpowder, is known by both names.

clue.text: Opposing a good one this month

parts.note: a means one, as in 'a hundred'
inst, short for instant, means this month in old business letters

explanation.surface: Someone resists a fine proposal made this month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inst' (instant) is old commercial shorthand for this month, as in 'your letter of the 5th inst'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in opposition to something is standing on the other side from it.

clue.text: English article is superior to the French passage

indicators.note: in a down entry being superior to means sitting above, so this comes first

parts.note: a is the English indefinite article
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Claims that an English writing is better than the French version.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'superior to' puts A IS above LE, the French for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkway between rows of seats, as in a church or theatre, is a gangway.

clue.text: How stupid can a board member be?

definitions.text: How stupid can a board member be?

parts.words: How stupid can a board member be?
parts.note: a board member is jokingly a plank of wood, and the question asks for the saying that compares a dim person to one

explanation.surface: Someone despairs of a dim company director.
explanation.walkthrough: A board member sounds like a company director, but a plank is a member of a board of wood; the British saying compares a dense person to one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means extremely dim, comparing the person to a thick wooden beam.

clue.text: Come out to see them before inviting leader of gang in

parts.note: 'em is a short informal form of them

indicators.note: inviting someone in takes them inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A host steps outside to meet guests before asking the gang's boss in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inviting' puts G, the first letter of 'gang', inside ERE after EM.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear or come into view is to step forth from somewhere hidden.

clue.text: Rash chap's going round Leeds after a riot

indicators.note: a piece going round another surrounds it, so it holds the other inside

parts.note: he's is short for he is, the chap being he

indicators.note: after a riot things are thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A reckless man tours Leeds in the aftermath of disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a riot' rearranges LEEDS to EDLES, and 'going round' puts HES round it. Leeds is a city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting carelessly without thought for consequences is reckless.
